runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1928 comes out as it did: Hoover wins, 444–87. The closest state was Rhode Island, which went to Smith by 0.6 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1920 and 1930 census counts interpolated to 1928 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1928 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

assumptions: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1928.
howIGotThis: What changed: Every adult can vote, and turns out.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: The country's doing well right now, and I like what they're promising for the farmers. But that Democrat fellow takes his religion seriously too, which matters to me.
south-white.controlQuote: The country's doing well right now, and I like what they're promising for the farmers. But that Democrat fellow takes his religion seriously too, which matters to me.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: The farm board sounds like it could help us get better prices. I worry about surpluses ruining everything we grow, and he says he'll protect our goods without the government taking over the farm itself.
women.controlQuote: The farm board sounds like it could help us get better prices. I worry about surpluses ruining everything we grow, and he says he'll protect our goods without the government taking over the farm itself.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: The fellow they've got running for the Democrats, he's Catholic—that's what folks keep saying bothers them. I'll stick with the Republican unless something changes by tomorrow.
